baseline.what_exists: ui2/frontend/src/brand/NexusWordmark.tsx draws into viewBox 0 0 220 72 and contains exactly three drawn children, in this order and with these literal values: a <text x="0" y="58" fontFamily={m3Theme.typography.fontFamily} fontSize="54" fontWeight="800" letterSpacing="-1" fill={color}> holding the characters ne; then <g transform="translate(66,6) scale(0.9)"><NexusXStrokes /></g>; then a <text x="132" y="58" ...same attributes...> holding the characters us. The width prop is computed as (height * 220) / 72 and height defaults to 40; color defaults to currentColor. ui2/frontend/src/brand/NexusXStrokes.tsx draws the X in a 64x64 box as exactly two paths and no more: <path d="M12 10 L24 10 L52 54 L40 54 Z" fill={NEXUS_X_TEAL} /> and <path d="M52 10 L40 10 L12 54 L24 54 Z" fill={NEXUS_X_BLUE} />. The x coordinates 0, 66 and 132 are the whole defect: they assume the string ne is exactly 66 units wide in whatever font the browser resolves from the theme stack.

report.objective: Make the neXus wordmark one piece of geometry that cannot drift with the rendering font. The Product Owner reports that on the login screen the mark reads as separated fragments -- 'ne', then a detached X, then 'us' -- instead of one word. The cause is in the component: the two letter groups are SVG text at fixed x coordinates while the X is at a fixed translate, so any font-metric difference between machines pulls the three pieces apart.
output_contract: A login screen whose product name reads as one word on any machine.
